articleTitle: Enhanced Cervical Cancer Diagnosis Using Advanced Transfer Learning Techniques
abstract: Cervical cancer poses a significant worldwide health obstacle for women, and timely identification is essential for effective treatment. Pap smear tests are a cost-effective and efficient screening method. However, the implementation of automated recognition and categorization of Pap smear cells can greatly improve the early detection of abnormalities. This research utilizes a transfer learning methodology, employing the fine-tuned Xception pre-trained model to identify and classify cervical cancer images with a training accuracy of 96.23% and a validation accuracy of 95.56%. The study also incorporates the Xception architecture, which leads to a decrease in processing resources while still achieving a high level of validation accuracy. The proposed framework underwent training and testing on the SipakMed dataset comprising 4049 high-resolution images. It achieved an accuracy of 95.70% in accurately differentiating between five categories of cervical cell samples. Utilizing transfer learning with the Xception model yields notable enhancements in both efficiency and accuracy, presenting a hopeful resolution for diagnosing cervical cancer, especially in situations with limited resources. This automated Pap smear cell classification development contributes to worldwide initiatives aimed at promoting women's health by improving early detection and perhaps saving lives through prompt intervention.

articleTitle: Empirical Method for Rice Grain Variety Classification
abstract: Rice is grown extensively worldwide and displays a wide genetic diversity., resulting in a variety of traits and characteristics across different types. In order to achieve realistic Rice Grain Classification., this research compared the use of Vgg19., MobileNet., MobileNet v2., CNN and DensNet algorithms. The data set used in this study collected from various data repositories such as kaggle.,GitHub.,VNMN and etc. The dataset comprises a total of 10.,000 high-resolution images of rice grains., with each image labeled according to its corresponding rice variety. The dataset included five distinct rice varieties: Akura., 1001., Konaram., MTU-64., and RNR. Each rice variety is represented by 2.,000 images in the dataset. Then CNN., Vgg19., MobileN et., MobileN et v2 and DensN et are trained and assessed using the enhanced dataset. Our research results revealed successful result with DenseN et emerging as the top performer., achieving an impressive accuracy of 96.87%. Following closely behind., MobileNet V2 demonstrated notable proficiency with a classification accuracy of 94.60%., while MobileNet and VGG 19 attained accuracies of 94 % and 90%., respectively.

articleTitle: IoT- Based Real- Time Medicine Reminder and Dispenser for Elderly Patients
abstract: People who follow a routine medication face a challenge when taking these medicines at regular intervals. It is observed that most older citizens face these problems if they have no one to take care of them. These people are not that smart to set reminders or alarms on their smartphones to remind them of their medication routines. A device such as an IoT-based Real-Time Medicine Reminder and Dispenser Robot can help these individuals. This device will have a reminder for each medicine the user might take by four methods, it will have a speaker that will call out the name of the medicine, a Display that shall show the name of the medicine, a dispenser system that will dispense the right medicine and a mobile notification will be send to the user's phone.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Assisted Power Factor Correction Using Capacitor Banks
abstract: Energy utilization and efficiency are currently recognized as the main goals in the electrical power industry. Power factor is frequently used to determine whether a system's power supply is good or bad. A drop in power factor may result from the need for electrical power system to power inductive loads in homes and businesses. The AC power system's power factor is a concern because AC power is widely used and there are many different types of loads, including inductive loads. A lower power factor in electric machines translates into reduced power consumption and efficiency. For efficiency to be higher, the power factor value must be near unity. A power factor correction system can increase and maintain the power factor value close to unity by utilizing a variety of compensation strategies. The system's power factor measurement, compensation, and output display were all managed using an Raspberry Pi. The input to the system was an AC power supply which was given to different types of loads. Capacitor banks were controlled with a relay module to solve the power factor issue with the help of machine learning algorithms. Because of this, the system's lagging inductive KVAR caused by lagging loads was eliminated, resulting in better power factor. The suggested solution will improve the electrical power system's efficiency and lower the losses. The study's conclusions demonstrate the considerable gains in power factor, energy loss reduction, and overall system performance optimization made possible by the suggested approach, which calls for the development of several capacitor bank stages in order to achieve the intended KVAR and guarantee the best possible use of capacitor banks.

articleTitle: An Efficient TinyVGG Model for Sugarcane Leaf Disease Classification in Precision Agriculture
abstract: Worldwide, sugarcane is an essential crop used to produce sugar and ethanol. However, several diseases, especially those that harm its leaves, pose serious obstacles to its production. The categorization of sugarcane leaf diseases is examined in this paper. A thorough grasp of disease categorization is essential for precise diagnosis and focused control measures in disease management methods. This abstract helps to build sustainable methods that seek to maintain sugarcane production and ensure the stability of the global sugarcane industries by clarifying the categorization of diseases that affect sugarcane leaves. A tiny VGG model is utilized in this article with varying numbers of epochs to obtain the highest accuracy and lowermost loss. Based on the available data, Epoch 20 has the lowest loss (0.6984 in the training phase and 0.8423 in the testing phase) and the best accuracy (0.7421 in the training phase and 0.6731 in the testing phase).

articleTitle: Implementation of Machine Learning in Battery Management System of Electric Vehicles
abstract: This research is based on ML (Machine Learning) based predictive modelling for assessing the SOC (State of Charge) of a BMS (Battery Management System). For the reliable and efficient use of a battery -based system, mainly in EVs, the accurate estimation of SOC is paramount. In this work, a secondary dataset including 93 samples of 4 key parameters namely Voltage, Current, Temperature, and SOC has been used to train the ML models for SOC estimation. The ML techniques which are implemented here in MATLAB are Linear Regression, and Support Vector Machine (SVM), for SOC prediction. 80 % of this dataset has been used for training and 20 % for testing. The Linear regression model provides a basic linear approach for SOC estimation. Whereas, the SVM has the ability of handling non-linear connection between input parameters and the output. The performance is compared on the basis of the test data inputs. Various graphical representations are also shown for illustrating the performance of developed models. The findings contribute significantly towards advancements in intelligent BMSs.

articleTitle: Multi-Protocol Conversion Unit Implementation on a FPGA
abstract: In this research paper, The Multi-Protocol Conversion Unit (MPCU), a testing design for MPCU to work on an FPGA and a 7-segment display driver is designed using Hardware Descriptive Language (HDL). The MPCU unit has the functionality of a converter and bridge that is it can take 8-bit inputs as soon as the device enables control is provided. Stores 8 different data on an MPCU RAM and operates according to the Data that is present in the MPCU RAM location 0. The MPCU uses protocols such as Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI) and Inter-Integrated Circuit (I2C). According to the operation mode, the device will perform one out of the seven modes described for MPCU. This device can perform data transfer to slaves from the micro controller or it can isolate the micro controller and transfer data from one slave to another without the micro controller accessing the data. Thus, we can have one single device for faster transfer of data to the protocols slave devices. The device is tested on a Numato Mimas spartan-6-based FPGA board. The design takes data from 8 switches as 8-bit data and stores it on the MPCU RAM at any moment when the data is pushed onto it by pressing the Push Data button. The output of SPI Test RAM and I2C Test RAM can be accessed via the 7-Segment display. To access this data from different locations of the Test RAM a separate Address Increment control is provided. Another switch is the Input (I) / Output (O) RAM switch can switch between the Input MPCU RAM, Output SPI Test RAM, and Output I2C Test RAM. This device has several benefits over the conventional SPI and I2C master individually.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of AHB to APB Bridge and AHB to UART Communication for SoC Integration
abstract: The AHB is a vital component in the AMBA family, deSigned to prioritize high performance, reduced power consumption, and efficient data transfer. Its main purpose is to facilitate communication between various system components. The APB is used to connect peripheral devices with lower data demands, employing a simple, non-pipelined protocol for data exchange between a master unit and multiple peripherals via a shared bus. This project focuses on implementing an RTL design of an AHB to APB bridge comprises of AHB slave interface, state machine and APB interface, including simulation of read and write operations. Furthermore, it also proposes integration of UART with the AHB interface by the FIFO buffer. This AHB to APB bridge enhances the functionality of System on Chip (SoC) configurations, especially those involving multiple masters and slaves, by effectively managing data transfers. Xilinx Vivado is utilized as the verification environment for this project, with Verilog as the chosen Hardware Description Language (HDL).

articleTitle: Hybrid Security Protocols: Bridging the Gap Between Efficiency and Security
abstract: This research explores the concept of a hybrid security protocol that combines the strengths of different existing protocols to safeguard digital communication. An ideal protocol should maintain a balance between security and efficiency, which is accomplished with the help of combining various algorithms. Hybrid security protocol takes advantage of both symmetric and asymmetric algorithms. A hybrid protocol developed using AES and ECC and an additional encryption method, which in terms provide a more efficient and secure protocol and is validated by performing experiments on the developed and the existing protocols. The results of the research work gives a detailed insights about the efficiency and security of the hybrid protocols.

articleTitle: Implementation of Sobel Edge Detection with Image Processing on FPGA
abstract: From laptop vision to medical diagnostics, picture processing is essential in lots of fields. In order to improve actual-time overall performance, this take a look at makes a speciality of applying the Sobel side detection technique on a Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) platform and taking advantage of its parallel processing abilities. One method this is regularly used to discover edges and lines in pics is known as Sobel side detection. Our recommended FPGA-based technique includes using a Hardware Description Language (HDL), which include Verilog, to layout and enforce a selected hardware structure. The layout uses Sobel convolution kernels to calculate gradient values and aspect importance through applying the kernels to photograph pixels in each horizontal and vertical orientations. Optimizing parallel processing for effective real-time performance is one of the maximum vital factors. After everything is completed, the display and photograph acquisition modules are included into the device. Performance evaluation includes measures like throughput, latency, and aid utilization to assure the effectiveness of the Sobel aspect detection machine primarily based on FPGA.

articleTitle: Advanced Traffic Signal Recognition Using Real-Time Detection Using YOLO v8
abstract: This study provides YOLOv8 for traffic signal recognition in the advanced version that takes place in a real- time environment for road safety improvement. Intensively and widely tested and trained, using the complex set of data, the YOLO v8 model gained a notable boost over its predecessors in the key performance metrics of precision, recall, and Fl-score. The system has done extremely well, with the Fl score being 90.18%. recall of 89.5% The error rates of natural and language translation are 5% and the precision of 91 %. 2% of errors. These desirable results indicate that this model could precisely and effectively classify the candidate of traffic signs in various weather and light conditions. This implies that inventions such as real-time traffic signal detection that YOLO v8 models pave the way for would be possible, thus increasing road safety and enhancing the reliability of autonomous driving systems.

articleTitle: Stock Market Forecasting Using LSTM
abstract: In this research paper, a novel methodology for forecasting stock market trends is presented: the utilization of Long Short-Term Memory networks, which are a part of RNN network. This model effectively incorporates the delivery of dynamic datasets, model training, and the immediate distribution of the learned TensorFlow model through the utilization of deep learning. The Long Short-Term Memory is a highly effective tool for understanding complex stock market behaviors, as it captures sequential dependencies and effortlessly adapts to changing market conditions. Transparency, collaboration, scalability, user experience, and security are given top priority in the project to guarantee accessibility for users of all levels of expertise. By outperforming conventional neural network architecture in prediction and by capturing dependencies over extended time periods, the LSTM model demonstrates its value. This research may pave the way for additional financial forecasting applications, thereby enhancing the efficacy of decision-making instruments in dynamic stock market environments.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis on Amazon Food Reviews using Machine Learning
abstract: Amazon food reviews refers to the feedback given by the users or customers who have purchased a certain food item from the Amazon platform. There are more than 500,000 reviews which help us to analyze and improve the current sentiment of the customers using the amazon products they have purchased and used. Here we have used 7 classifiers on the given dataset on Amazon fine food reviews from Kaggle. Our experiment results showed that we have the highest accuracy when using Logistic Regression and SGD with 94.342% with TFIDF and BOW respectively. Other classifiers also come close to this accuracy using BOW and TFIDF in our research. We have also used BERT and GloVe and LSTM for further analysis. All this is done by dividing the dataset into positive and negative reviews. Taking a scale of 5 to rate the given products we can identify if the customer likes their used products or not.

articleTitle: Cotton Leaf Disease Classification Using Fine-Tuned VGG16 Deep Learning Model
abstract: Textile production plays a critical role in agriculture worldwide, and the cotton crop, which is the basis of this industry, suffers greatly from leaf diseases that are often very destructive and cause economic losses. This study presents a novel approach to the classification of four major cotton leaf diseases: Employing an exclusive VGG16 fine-tuned deep learning model to diagnose and evaluate cotton plant diseases such as Cotton Bacterial Blight, Verticillium Wilt, Fusarium Wilt, and Cotton Leaf Curl Disease. We employed a leaf image dataset to span a vast spectrum of signs symptoms conditions to pre-train and fine-tune the model. By performing diligent pre-training involving image augmentation and model adjustment for the particular task of cotton leaf disease detection, we found that VGG16 architecture is flexible enough to apply to our case. The model's performance was subject to a thorough assessment with the help of a different testing dataset proving the accuracy of a total classification of 93.8%. Precision score, recall score, and F1 score metrics also enlighten us that the model can accurately detect and classify the disease. The study reflects the possibility of creating the medium for fine-tuned deep-learning models in agricultural areas that represent an integral and efficient instrument for early disease detection and management. The results illuminated the actual consequences, and pathway for improvement of farm monitoring, minimized economic losses, and suggested support for sustainable farming practices. Future research will look into many dimensions: creating a bigger dataset, implementing other sophisticated architectures, and finally implementing real-world agricultural applications using the mentioned models.

articleTitle: Employing Machine Learning for Effective Lung Cancer Diagnosis
abstract: People all over the world are affected by Lung Cancer. Its timely prediction is important in prolonging patients' lives. This research paper proposes a model to improve the success rate of timely predictions. The authors have utilized the dataset from Kaggle to evaluate experiments. The dataset has records of 309 patients. To improve the accuracy of the model, class balancing using SMOTE was applied by the authors. Classifiers used by the authors in this research were Random Forest (RF), Ada Boost, k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and Gaussian Naive Bayes (GNB). Accuracy, Sensitivity, Precision, and F measures have been utilized to evaluate the performance of the proposed model. This model obtained the highest accuracy, i.e., 100% within the confines of the test data using the RF classifier.

articleTitle: Deep Learning in Agriculture: Convolutional Neural Network-Based Classification of Potato Diseases for Enhanced Crop Management
abstract: Global food security is greatly enhanced by potatoes, which are a staple crop in every country. Potato leaf diseases, however, represent a serious risk to agricultural productivity and the stability of the economy. For diseases like early blight, late blight, and septoria blight to inflict as much damage as possible, early detection and prompt action are essential. Based on image processing methods, a model based on a convolutional neural network (CNN) in this paper for the automated categorization of illnesses affecting potato leaves has been proposed. The proposed model effectively distinguishes between normal and abnormal circumstances by identifying and detecting illness symptoms in potato leaves, utilizing deep learning capabilities. After extensive testing and analysis, our CNN model ranks potato leaf photos into three classes with an astounding 98.99% accuracy rate for healthy, early, and late blight. On the other hand, potato leaf diseases present a serious risk. This high degree of precision provides important information for crop protection and sustainable agriculture methods, highlighting the efficacy and promise of CNN-based approaches in the early diagnosis and treatment of potato diseases.

articleTitle: Classification of Shells and Pebbles Using CNN with MobileNetV2 Transfer Learning
abstract: The research paper provides a detailed analysis of shell and pebble classification using a convolutional neural network (CNN) approach with the MobileNetV2 transfer learning model. The dataset, containing 4,324 images, was carefully gathered and separated into different sets for training, validation, and testing purposes. The suggested CNN design, which efficiently utilizes MobileNetV2 for feature extraction, underwent training for 80 epochs. It demonstrated a steady and significant reduction in loss along with a notable improvement in accuracy. Through the validation and testing phases, the model's robustness and generalization capabilities were further confirmed, demonstrating high precision and recall for both shell and pebble classes. The results highlight the effectiveness and practicality of transfer learning in image classification tasks, especially in distinguishing between objects with subtle visual distinctions like shells and pebbles, providing valuable insights for future studies in related fields.

articleTitle: Exploring Rhubarb Diversity: Categorizing Three Classes Using a Combined CNN-PCA Model
abstract: To develop agronomic methods and classify crops, the innovation of the machine learning tool would facilitate the agricultural community to accomplish the task. The current paper proposes a new hybrid model that applies Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) together with Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to process the rhubarbs classification process accurately and efficiently. Research of this model embraces three of the types: Victorian, Crimson Red, and Ruby. Specifically, the research utilizes the extraction robust feature capabilities of CNN and the efficient dimensionality reduction technique of PCA. Using a complete rhubarb leaf data set the model was trained, validated, and tested. The model was shown to be more accurate, precise, and recalling, than both traditional CNN models and other prevalent machine learning schemes. This study revealed that the multi-channel CNN-PCA hybrid model can not only pinpoint the discreet shape differences among plant varieties that are closely related, but it may also perform better than the existing classification methodologies. The experimental data not only broadens the view of computational botany providing a precise and reliable tool for plant variety classification, but it also creates a new trend in the agriculture sector of using hybrid machine learning models as a preliminary research phase. With the assistance of correct and swift identification of plant species, our proposed scheme is reflected as a means capable of strengthening biodiversity conservation programs, improving precision agriculture, and also promoting sustainable farming approaches. In line with this, the next research mistakes include: scaling up the model to other crops and incorporating it into digital agriculture platforms for actual-world use. Such a research activity illustrates the groundbreaking character of the application of machine learning techniques, enabling the progress of agricultural science and also humans' understanding of plant variability.

articleTitle: Analyzing VANET Performance in Urban Environments: A Comparative Analysis of Propagation Models with OLSR-Based Vehicular Networks through SUMO and NS3
abstract: In the realm of technological progress, vehicular communication plays a pivotal role in the context of contemporary urbanization. The efficacy of Vehicular Ad hoc Networks (VANETs) is predominantly influenced by routing protocols and propagation models. This study delves into the real-time impact of various propagation models on VANET performance, recognizing the dynamic and challenging nature of vehicular environments. The selection of an accurate propagation model is crucial for establishing reliable communication, especially in urban settings. This research assesses and compares the performance of widely used propagation models, including Free Space Path Loss (FSPL), ITU-R P.1411 Loss Model and Nakagami fading, within the context of an Optimized Link State Routing (OLSR) based VANET. The study considers diverse real-time traffic scenarios in the urban environment. Performance metrics such as Average Routing Throughput, Packet Delivery Ratio and End-to-End Delay are meticulously examined using both SUMO and NS3 platforms. Notably, the study underscores the limitations of a fixed propagation model and advocates for the dynamic adaptation of propagation models based on specific scenarios. The network parameter comparison highlights the better performance scenarios that are possible with the combination of the FSPL and ITU-R P.1411 propagation models with the OLSR protocol.

articleTitle: Unbalanced Ternary Inverter Implementations in CNTFET Technology
abstract: Modern digital technology utilizes binary digital logic to transfer the information, which is quite exhaustive and leads to more area exploitation as, due to the base-2 in binary logic, a greater number of interconnects are being used to pass the information. Researchers are trying to explore the higher base values to be used in digital integrated circuits (ICs), i.e., multi-valued logic, which comes with base-3, base-4, or higher. The multi-valued logic provides a greater number of input iterations to pass on the logic information, hence reducing the number of interconnect to transmit approximately similar information as binary logic. Carbon nanotube field effect transistor (CNTFET) can manipulate different threshold voltage values by changing the chirality of nanotubes being used as channels in the device. In this paper, the existing CNTFET -based ternary logic cells are reviewed and compared for different performance metrics.

articleTitle: Improving Mango Quality Assessment: A Multi-Layer Perceptron Approach for Grading
abstract: The quality standard of an agricultural product, which is often mango, one of the most popular foods in my country, performs a critical function of selecting the best from the market and providing the highest satisfaction to the consumers. Checking the quality for a long time is still difficult because it uses manual inspection and simple mechanical devices, which can't ensure that the evaluation is consistent, objective, and efficient. This study comes up with a new method of mango quality evaluation that relies on a Multi-Layer Perception (MLP) network-the most powerful artificial neural network with the ability to perform pattern recognition and classification tasks well. The model was developed and trained on a dataset comprising both external and internal quality attributes of mangoes, classified into four quality levels: The Genius category is the highest one, followed by the Excellent, the Good, and the last category Fair. MLP showed excellent performance in this aspect, achieving 95.7% general classifiable precision, which far exceeds the traditional methods with the highlighting of machine learning as the method that could push the assessment of fruit quality to the other level. This study, not only, involved the investigation of the feasibility and efficiency of MLP models for the evaluation purpose of agricultural quality, but also, it proposed new directions for future studies such as data of sensory influences and broadening of scope to other products of agriculture. The report points to one of the most important positive aspects of the experiment in terms of a more trustworthy assessment of quality with further selection of the producers, dealers, and buyers in the agricultural chain.

articleTitle: Using Daily Mean outside Temperature to Define Consumption Patterns
abstract: To produce intelligent structures, it is essential to identify and recognise patterns in the context of construction. In this situation, giving the systems the ability to learn and make judgements is crucial. The difficulty is predicting human behaviour inside the structure using the identified element. Due to user weather adaptation, the daily mean outside temperature is one of the factors that affects human comfort. In this study, cluster methods were used to examine how much energy was consumed in a workplace in relation to the ambient temperature and the daily mean temperature. You can forecast consumption using the cluster.

articleTitle: Fusion of Multimodal Biometrics for Improved Palm Recognition Using Image Processing
abstract: This study presents an advanced multimodal biometric system that utilizes 2DLPP and Local Binary Pattern (LBP) to extract features by addressing the deficiencies of current approaches to meet the growing demand for dependable palmprint identification systems. The methodology employs noise elimination and Competitive Hand Valley Detection (CHVD) as preprocessing stages to obtain the ROI. By utilizing adaptive feature fusion, our approach permits the adjustment of the weights of LBP and 2DLPP features in real time. The evaluation system of the matching stage has been revised to improve discrimination capabilities. The proposed method obtains a Genuine Acceptance Rate (GAR) of 99.2% in palmprint recognition using the CASIA Multi-Spectral Database v1.0 as a benchmark which is better and more efficient compared to traditional techniques.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Emotion Recognition by Fusion of Facial Expressions and Speech Features
abstract: The swift progress in emotion recognition technology has resulted in the creation of a greatly cohesive human-computer interaction experience. This research introduces two approaches to the emotion recognition: one based on analyzing facial expressions and the other on analyzing speech. By leveraging the complementary nature of facial expressions and speech, we utilize Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to learn facial emotion features and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to extract speech emotion features. Concurrently, we employ multiple small-scale kernels within a convolution block to capture various aspects of facial expression, while the LSTM model is employed to extract significant features from speech. Subsequently, a fusion technique is applied to combine facial expression and speech features, allowing us to accurately determine the emotion conveyed in a video. The effectiveness of the facial emotion recognition model is assessed using the FER 2013 and CK + datasets, while the voice emotion recognition model is evaluated using the RAVDESS dataset. The fusion model has got an accuracy of 69%.

articleTitle: Vision Sense: Real-Time Object Detection And Audio Feedback System For Visually Impaired Individuals
abstract: This project introduces a transformative object detection system designed to enhance the navigational capabilities of visually impaired individuals through the application of advanced computer vision technologies. Utilizing the You Only Look Once (YOLO) model, paired with the Comprehensive Object Collection (COCO) dataset, this system provides real-time, accurate object detection and classification. The core functionality of the application allows for the processing of both static images and live video feeds, enabling blind users to receive auditory announcements of nearby objects, thereby assisting with spatial awareness and environmental interaction. The system leverages a pre-trained YOLO model to ensure robust detection performance, achieving a peak detection accuracy of 99%. By delivering object labels and bounding box coordinates audibly, the application serves as a critical tool in improving the daily independence and quality of life for people with visual impairments. This project not only highlights the potential of deep learning in assistive technologies but also underscores the importance of adaptive solutions in inclusive technology development.

articleTitle: Predicting Cervical Cancer with Deep Learning: Comparative Analysis of VGGNet, GoogleNet, and DenseNet121 Models
abstract: The proposed study compares the efficacy, degree of accuracy, and computational efficiency of three deep learning algorithms, namely, VGGNet, GoogleNet, and DenseNet121, in terms of their capacity to determine cervical cancer from smear images and thus further the role of artificial intelligence in medical tests. The analysis that we conducted quantitatively was on a dataset of cervical smear images annotated with labels such as normal, pre-cancerous, and cancerous. The data set is preprocessed by conducting image resizing, augmentation, and normalizing the data. For each model, I used TensorFlow and Keras frameworks, which were built with cervical cancer in mind. During the training, it splits the data in the training, validation, and test set and monitors the performance with accuracy, precision, recall, Fl-score, and AUC. A qualitative analysis told apart the models based on these metrics in terms of training time and model complexity. DenseNet121 excelled in all image segmentation tasks with the highest accuracy (93%)., precision (90%)., recall (95%), F1-score (92.5%), and AUC (0.97). GoogleNet, although slightly less accurate, was nevertheless the method employing the shortest training time and the least complexity. In this way, it becomes a viable choice for limited resource settings. VGGNet used a little bit, but it did give important ideas about model depth's influence on medical image quality. It furthermore brought to the issue of accuracy-computational demand tradeoffs of the models.

articleTitle: Advancing Human Resource Strategies with Deep Learning: Predictive Analytics for Improving Employee Retention Rates
abstract: This research paper deals with deep learning technologies in improving human resource (HR) strategies. However, the emphasis is put on predictive analytics, which is applied to raise the retention rates of employees. Through the use of a deep feedforward neural network, the researchers investigate a variety of datasets containing among others attributes concerning demographics, job performance, engagement, and turnover for several large organizations. The research will be the mixed-method approach, which combines quantitative approaches to apply the predictive models by practical applicability from HR professionals and employees. The outcomes show that deep learning has a remarkably high level of efficiency over traditional predictive models and it produces higher accuracies, precisions, recalls, and F1 scores in predicting employee turnover. This points out the fact that deep learning could be the future of HR analytics because it allows for building more accurate and earlier forecasts and so it entails management strategies that are oriented to the retention of valuable HR. Despite this, the use of these highly sophisticated systems poses significant ethical issues like those of data privacy and the transparency of algorithms, which the study discusses concretely.

articleTitle: Medical Image Processing, Disease Prediction and Report Summarization Using Generative Adversarial Networks and AIML
abstract: Imagine if technology could help doctors see clearer and predict diseases earlier. That's what this project is all about. We're combining two powerful technologies, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AIML), to shake up how we handle medical images and reports. First up, we're using GANs to make medical images sharper and more useful. Thinkof it like giving doctors super-clear glasses to spot details that might be hard to see otherwise. Then, we're using AIML to predict diseases by looking at these images and other patient info. It's like having a crystal ball that helps doctors catch problems before they get serious. But that's not all. We're also creating a smart system that writes brief but super-helpfulsummaries of these medical reports. It's like having an assistant who reads all the details and pulls out the most important parts, making it easier for doctors to decide what's next. By bringing together these technologies, we're not just making diagnoses more accurate and predicting diseases sooner, but we're also making sure doctors get the key info they need quickly. It's all about making healthcare smarter and more efficient for everyone involved especially for elderly and especially abled people.

articleTitle: Enhancing Energy Efficiency in Commercial Office Buildings: A Smart IoT and Machine Vision Approach
abstract: Commercial office buildings often waste substantial energy due to the inefficient use of HVAC and lighting systems. This paper introduces an innovative Internet of Things (IoT) and Machine Vision-based system to combat this issue and improve energy efficiency. The system combines real-time occupancy detection using the You Only Look Once (YOLO) object detection method with CCTV footage obtained through the ESP32 cam module. Additionally, machine vision technology evaluates ambient light conditions. Leveraging the gathered occupancy and lighting data, the system autonomously controls lighting and employs a novel algorithm to regulate HVAC activation for cooling, factoring in indoor and outdoor temperatures. Our approach achieved an impressive accuracy rate of 96.31%. Specifically designed for office environments where occupants typically prioritize energy conservation less, this system offers a discreet solution that dynamically adjusts to real-time occupancy patterns. By implementing this system, commercial buildings have the potential to reduce energy consumption while ensuring occupant comfort is maintained significantly.

Author Keywords: You Only Look Once (YOLO) object detection method

articleTitle: Low Power VLSI Architecture for Variable Gain Amplifier Using Pseudo Current Steering Gain Tuning Method
abstract: This project introduces four variable-gain amplifiers (VGAs) that utilize a novel pseudo-current-steering gain-tuning technique. In the VGA1, a standalone gain control block is implemented using a single-voltage-controlled dual- branch Current copying circuit. The VGA2 integrates two NMOS transistors biased by a variable voltage into a conventional common-source amplifier to divert a portion of the entire current. The third and fourth VGA's are similar to VGA 1 and VGA 2. In third and fourth architectures namely Design-I and Design-II we aim to expand the concept by implementing the Power gating technique to reduce power consumption. Low-power techniques refer to strategies employed in electronic design to mitigate the power consumption of integrated circuits (ICs) and electronic systems.

articleTitle: A Novel Model of Prepayment for E-Commerce Business in the Context of Bangladesh
abstract: E-commerce irregularities are increasing constantly. The objective of this paper is to find various irregularities in e-commerce business and work on the most frequent irregularities. Online payment issue has been observed as the most noticeable occurrence in the current context. Customers (both buyers and sellers) are constantly suffering from it. This paper identifies the problems related to this and proposes a new model to overcome the issues. Data are collected through online survey and the result (more than 91 %) shows the acceptance of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Making Authenticated Key Exchange Protocols More Secure with One-Way Hash Functions
abstract: The safety of key alternate protocols is predicated closely on cozy cryptographic algorithms and protocols. But, maximum of these protocols are liable to assault. To increase the safety of those protocols, a unique technique has been proposed - utilizing one-way hash capabilities. A one-way hash characteristic is a set of rules that takes an enter, and produces a hard and fast-period output or hash price. This output is specific for the respective enter and almost impossible to be reversed. Using one-manner hash functions has been proposed for making authenticated key trade protocols more comfortable. In an average authenticated key change protocol, the proverb begins by means of sending a one-manner hash of the keys, and the verifier then exams this hash to verify that it's far correct. If the hash value fits, the verifier can finish that the secret's legitimate. By using one-manner hash capabilities, the verifier may be sure that the important thing trade has been accomplished securely, as an attacker might no longer be able to generate the proper hash or guess the important thing. This approach prevents any malicious activity earlier than the protocol is hooked up, because the hash could be invalid and the important thing change now not viable. Moreover, one-way hash capabilities can also be used to securely transmit passwords.

articleTitle: Machine Learning with Color and Multispectral Images: Comparative Analysis of Approaches
abstract: Machine studying with colour and multispectral photographs is used for an expansion of applications, which includes object reputation, image segmentation, and image type. The mission of extracting significant data from those photographs is complicated by way of their complexity and diversity. Various facts, fashions, and computational processes are used to seize the spectral and spatial characteristics of the image. This paper provides: A comparative evaluation of existing techniques for device-gaining knowledge of colour and multispectral photographs, focusing on the application of colour augmentation, Picture filtering, Convolutional neural networks. First, we talk about recent applications of coloration augmentation and photo filtering techniques. We then present a detailed dialogue of the diverse architectures of convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which are used for the challenge of system learning with colour and multispectral photos. Sooner or later, we illustrate how these approaches can be combined with a view to gain higher effects on one-of-a-kind datasets. This paper is aimed at providing a general overview of the different processes for machine mastering with coloration and multispectral pictures, with a focus on the chosen software areas in which promising effects were received.

articleTitle: Advanced Classification of Indian Turnip Varieties using CNN and Naive Bayes Techniques in Precision Agriculture
abstract: The ever-raising need for food safety and environmentally friendly farming triggers the mechanism of applying precision agriculture technologies. There are some of these techniques but none are as important as machine learning and deep learning techniques in a crop classification and management enhancements touch. The present research is devoted to turnip differentiation among three Indian major varieties- ‘Pusa Swarnima’, ‘Purple Top White Globe’, and ‘Snowball’ -that are going to apply Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and the simplest of Bayesian model. Although a comprehensive dataset was obtained from the turnip pictures by applying different preprocessing techniques and the models were designed for this purpose, the classification was performed using only visual and phenotypic characteristics. There was the evaluation of the model performance using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score metrics. It was discovered by us that the deep learning in CNN-CNN brought a high level of precision agriculture revolution since CNN proved to be better in the turnip varieties classification, rather than compared to naive Bayes, which showed a not appropriate solution. The study shows the usefulness of CNN and Naive Bayes models for broad bean variety identification and even offers to investigate the use of these technologies in the development of agricultural information systems. Discovering and advancing crop kinds categorization techniques has a huge role in the optimal application of farming methods. In the end, it can assist in growing more, higher quality, and more sustainable crops.

articleTitle: Optimizing Pneumonia Detection: Integrating Quadratic Discriminant Analysis and Deep Q-Networks Through Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has shown its relevance in the medical world in the last years getting the most improved results in the diagnosis and therapy of diseases. For this study, it tries to use RL methods, particularly DQN drastically with QDA in an attempt to improve pneumonia diagnosis, and decision making in healthcare. The research applies a dataset that consists of 5863 x-ray images on chest especially those mainly concerned pneumonia cases. The mentioned achievement in pneumonia classification was obtained by joining the QDA and DQN models, resulting in outstanding performance metrics. Moreover, both approaches, namely, the QDA and the DQN, are worth considering, as they not only managed to classify the data appropriately but also yielded the specified performance metrics. The model proved itself to be pretty precise with-it precision, recall, and F1 score values being 95.2%, 97.8%, and 96.5% respectively and accuracy being 96.5%. These results reaffirm that this proposal can be of great value in helping doctors to identify patients with pneumonia and in improving their outcomes as well as the healthcare system efficiency. Study's long-term expectations include deployment of QAD-DQN into more fields of medical diagnosis with attempt to make it work better. Altogether, the achievement of the fusion of qualitative and deep reinforcement learning gives a chance of a new milestone in the decision-making of healthcare, with a prospect of bright future in the diagnostic performance and treatment of medical problems.

articleTitle: Leveraging AI and ML for Predictive Analysis and Feature Attribution in Abnormal Network Behavior Detection
abstract: India has witnessed 15% increase in cyber-attacks in 2023 since 2022. Aadhar data breach is one of example among many cyber-attacks in India that cause millions of citizens to lose the personal details such as name, phone number, address, Aadhar number to hackers. Covid 19 of 500 million people were leaked by hacker is the second example faced by Indian organization in medical domain. There was a need to overcome the limitation of current security method organization have imposed Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) to stop the cyber-attacks on Indian organization. With AI and ML model observe the patterns in the data and predict the trends in data and with continuous monitoring identifies the abnormal attacks. The aim of this paper is to find the contribution of attributes / features in dataset towards prediction of abnormal behavior in the network. Model uses SelectKBest() method to select the best feature among the other attributes. These attributes act as inputs to support vector machine that uses linear kernel to predict the attacks. The model archives an accuracy of 97% and Shapley additive explanations is used to explain feature contribution.

articleTitle: AI-Based Daily, Weekly and Monthly Rain Forecasting by using Different Time Series Models
abstract: This work focuses on the comprehensive exploration and forecasting of daily rainfall, a crucial element in weather prediction and environmental planning. We amalgamated two time series datasets spanning from 2013 to 2022, encompassing vital meteorological parameters such as dry bulb temperature, maximum and minimum temperature, humidity, and rainfall (in mm) for each day. The primary objectives were to evaluate the data's characteristics through Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and visualizations, identifying non-stationary patterns, and subsequently applying advanced forecasting models. Initially, we employed Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) to capture the temporal dynamics and seasonality inherent in the data. Subsequently, deep learning emerged as a promising avenue for time series forecasting. Leveraging Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, a type of recurrent neural network (RNN), we aimed to capture intricate temporal dependencies for enhanced rainfall prediction. Additionally, a comparative analysis was conducted by employing SARIMA in tandem with Rolling Forecast, emphasizing the model's adaptability to evolving patterns. This approach sought to harness the combination of traditional time series methods and the robust predictive capabilities of deep learning. Our study unfolds a multifaceted approach to rainfall forecasting, elucidating the strengths and limitations of SARIMA and LSTM models. Through EDA, modeling, and comparative analysis, we illuminate the intricate patterns within the time series data. The results and insights derived from this study provide valuable contributions to the field of meteorological forecasting, offering a nuanced understanding of the methodologies employed and their respective efficacies.

articleTitle: Exploring the Effectiveness of MobileNet50 Convolutional Neural Network Transfer Learning for Accurate Land Cover Classification in High-Resolution Satellite Imagery
abstract: Interpreting satellite pictures is crucial in remote sensing applications due to the increasing demand for automated solutions. This study attempts to fulfill the need for precise and efficient interpretation methods by employing modern deep learning models., specifically such as MobileNet., for categorizing satellite images. The article discusses challenges in existing benchmark datasets for analyzing remote sensing photos and introduces a new dataset called “Satellite Image Classification Dataset-RSI-CB256.,” comprising four distinct classes derived from sensors and Google Maps images. The proposed approach utilizes transfer learning and the capabilities of pre-trained MobileNet 50 architecture to extract intricate characteristics from satellite photos. The dataset undergoes thorough preparation., involving techniques like as data augmentation., scaling., and normalization., to enhance the robustness of the model. Comparative studies demonstrate the effectiveness of MobileN et in capturing intricate patterns in the diverse sample. MobileNet achieves outstanding performance with a precision of 98.93%., showcasing its ability to efficiently utilize resources in various applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Leukemia Diagnosis: A Deep Learning Approach for Subtype Classification
abstract: Accurate classification of leukemia subtypes from microscopic images is crucial for treatment decisions and prognostic assessments. Manual methods are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and prone to inter-observer variability, necessitating automated systems. Traditional machine learning relies on manual feature extraction, while deep learning employs CNNs for end-to-end learning from raw image data. Existing methodologies struggle with achieving high accuracy due to subtle morphological differences between leukemia subtypes. Traditional methods may lack robustness and generalization capability, resulting in suboptimal performance. To address these challenges, we introduce a novel deep learning-based approach for automated leukemia subtype classification. Leveraging state-of-the-art CNN architectures and transfer learning, our model aims to enhance accuracy, robustness, and generalization. We utilize transfer learning with a pre-trained Efficient-NetV2-s architecture and the fastai library for efficient model development. Data preprocessing techniques such as image resizing, normalization, and augmentation further improve performance. Experimental results showcase our model's efficacy, achieving over 93% accuracy on a validation dataset.

articleTitle: Implementation of Fuzzy MPPT for Grid Connected PV – Wind – Battery System
abstract: The integration of renewable energy sources like photovoltaic (PV) and wind power into the grid necessitates efficient management strategies to optimize their performance and ensure grid stability. This paper proposes a novel approach by combining PV, wind, and battery energy storage systems (BESS) with a fuzzy Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm. The integration of these diverse sources aims to enhance energy reliability and minimize reliance on conventional fossil fuel-based power generation. The fuzzy MPPT algorithm offers adaptability to varying environmental conditions, thereby maximizing energy capture from both PV and wind sources. By dynamically adjusting the operating points of the PV and wind systems, the algorithm optimizes power generation while ensuring smooth integration with the grid. Moreover, the inclusion of a BESS facilitates energy storage to mitigate intermittent issues inherent in renewable sources and enables better management of supply-demand imbalances. Through simulations and experimental validation, this study evaluates the performance of the proposed system under different operating conditions and grid scenarios. The presented system is simulated in MATLAB and the results demonstrate the effectiveness of the fuzzy MPPT algorithm in enhancing the overall efficiency and stability of the grid-connected PV and wind system with battery storage. This research contributes to the advancement of renewable energy integration technologies, offering a promising solution for sustainable power generation and grid management in the transition towards a cleaner energy future.

articleTitle: Utilization of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Visual Effects
abstract: The research on computer vision mainly aims to enable computers to understand and interpret images. Computer vision is an emerging discipline, and applying generative artificial intelligence technology to image processing is an important entry point in current machine vision research. When generating images, this article utilized adversarial learning mechanisms to optimize the parameters of the generator and discriminator, creating a competitive relationship between the two and gradually improving the quality of the generated images. Adversarial training methods were used in video processing to optimize the generated model, enabling it to map between different styles and achieve style transfer. The generative adversarial network was optimized using a cyclic consistency loss function to ensure consistency of video content before and after editing. Based on the trained recurrent generative adversarial network, style transformation and content editing on the video were performed. The PSNR value of generated image 3 was 27.1; the PSNR (peak signal-to-noise ratio) value of the original image was 27.8; the SSIM (Structural Similarity) value of the generated image was 0.95; the SSIM value of the original image was 1.00. The PSNR and SSIM values of the generated image with image number 3 in the experiment were relatively high and close to the corresponding values of the original image. This article provided a reference for the research on the application of generative artificial intelligence in visual effects.

articleTitle: Novel CNN Architecture for Accurate Glaucoma Detection: Evaluation and Insights
abstract: Glaucoma is a major cause of permanent blindness worldwide, and early detection is essential to avoid the advancement of the disease and loss of vision. A new Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) structure is presented in this research to improve the precision of glaucoma identification using fundus pictures. We used a dataset of 6682 images and split it 80–20 for training and testing our model, with an emphasis on achieving high precision and recall rates. The CNN design consists of 10 layers, carefully organized to detect the complex patterns associated with glaucomatous optic neuropathy. The experimental results show remarkable performance, with precision scores of 0.999 for glaucoma and 0.935 for non-glaucoma, recall rates of 0.942 and 0.998, F1-scores of 0.970 and 0.966, and specificities of 0.998 and 0.942, respectively for glaucoma and non-glaucoma class. The model attained an accuracy of 96.78 %, weighted precision of 96.98 %, weighted recall of 96.78 %, weighted F1-score of 96.79 %, and weighted specificity of 97.28 %. The results are showing encouraging potential for incorporating deep learning technologies in ocular diagnostic processes.

articleTitle: Improved Celery Variety Classification in India Using CNN-KNN Hybrid Model
abstract: Classification of celery varieties plays a primary role as an essential factor of agriculture that works towards increasing productivity and sustainability. Age-old methods, though at times laborious and error-prone, are sometimes, the most efficient and reliable. This study reveals a fresh perspective on celery variety classification in India, employing a Human Hybrid Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) - K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) architecture to blend the strengths of deep learning and instance-based learning. This integration will prominently enhance the accuracy of results. A uniform dataset of celery images was created including a wide diversity of growth stages and conditions; this dissimilar dataset has been applied to this CNN-KNN hybrid model. Our model was trained, developed, and tested rigorously, therefore it showed a remarkable improvement (94%) in classification accuracy in this respect to existing methods. The discovery validates the work of the hybrid model in correctly classifying the celery varieties giving huge progress to the machine learning (ML) use in farming. The study demonstrates that the cassette network and k-nearest neighbor approach are promising for crop variety classification, which motivates future research into precision agriculture methods. The study not only provides a hint for better management of similar technologies but also indicates the usefulness of the hybrid ML models in pressing issues in the agricultural sector.

articleTitle: Blood Cell Detection and Counting Using Deep Learning
abstract: Manual blood cell counting in microscopic images is a laborious and error-prone task that poses significant challenges in healthcare diagnostics and hematology research. The traditional method not only consumes valuable time but also introduces the task of human error, potentially leading to inaccurate results and delayed patient care. To address these challenges, this project presents an automated blood cell Identification and Enumeration system built on the YOLO (You Only Look Once) algorithm. This innovative solution aims to revolutionize blood cell analysis by leveraging cutting-edge deep learning technology. By automating the process, it significantly reduces the time required on blood cell counting and minimizes the possibility for human errors. The System detects and classifies various blood cell types, including red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets, with high accuracy and efficiency. Moreover, it offers a user-friendly interface for healthcare professionals and researchers, facilitating easy input of microscopic images and providing real-time detection results. Preliminary results indicate a detection accuracy of 97.2%, showcasing the system's reliability. This project holds the potential to transform the landscape of hematology, enhancing the speed and precision of blood cell analysis, ultimately improving patient care and advancing scientific understanding in the field of hematology.

articleTitle: Innovations in Inhaler Technology: Advancing Medication Delivery Devices
abstract: The Inhaler represents a cornerstone in the management of respiratory health, having undergone meticulous testing and comprehensive analysis of user feedback. This abstract serves to distil the noteworthy attributes extolled by participants in the testing phase, emphasizing its capacity to house four capsules simultaneously, its ergonomically crafted design fostering ease of use and its straightforward operational mechanism. Furthermore, it delineates specific areas identified by respondents for potential improvement, such as fortifying the resilience of the mouthpiece hinge, honing needle sharpness to facilitate seamless piercing, and enhancing the tactile grip of the device's button. Despite these constructive criticisms, participants retain an optimistic outlook regarding the Inhaler's capacity for refinement and its pivotal contribution to the advancement of respiratory healthcare. This abstract underscores the mutually beneficial collaboration between users and developers, which serves as a catalyst for innovation and the evolution of medical device technology.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Video Coding Using Neural Network-Based Non-Local Transform
abstract: Excessive-efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) is a vital technique used to reduce the scale of video files at the same time as offering improved video pleasure. Conventionally, HEVC achieves this reduction through additives along with the spatial, temporal, and remodel coding gear. A unique method to enhance the coding performance of HEVC, in addition, has been proposed through the deployment of a neural community-primarily based non-nearby transform (NL-T). The NL-T is a more advantageous transform rather than the conventional transform prediction mode. Its miles prepared with a progressed non-local-enabling block matching set of rules and deep getting-to-know based totally channel coding., an NL-T block is assigned to each macro block and is then trained to manner and encodes inter-pixel dependencies for advanced coding gain. The performance of NL-T is evaluated through assessment with the heuristic block matching algorithm, in which it's far discovered that the NL-T achieves up to five.2dB of development in terms of peak signal-to-noise Ratio (PSNR) for a given bitrate. This paper demonstrates how the NL-T can drastically enhance HEVC coding performance as compared to conventional methods.

articleTitle: Battery and Supercapacitor FED BLDC Motor for EV Applications
abstract: This research uses simulation to investigate the viability and capacity of a hybrid energy storage system (HESS), which consists of battery and super-capacitor units. Over the past 20 years, there has been a significant increase in the price of petrol due to the extensive usage of internal combustion engine (ICE)-based cars, which has had a detrimental impact on the environment and accelerated the depletion of fossil fuel supplies. Due to these difficulties as well as the poor efficiency of traditional drivetrains, the automative industry is now seriously considering and pursuing drivetrain electrification in automotive systems. In Electric motors that are fueled by onboard energy storage systems provide all or some of the propulsion in electrified vehicles. To address the shortcomings of current energy storage devices and further the drive towards vehicle electrification, the HESS topology was selected with consideration for cost, performance, and the ease of use of power and control circuits. The necessary power, converter losses, energy storage device constraints, and battery cell current quality are all taken into account in the design.

Author Keywords: battery and super capacitor HESS (BLDC) drive

articleTitle: Development of Microcontroller-Based BLDC Motor Speed Controller for EV
abstract: The Arduino UNO-based BLDC motor controller project demonstrates the successful integration of hardware and software components to achieve efficient motor control for electric vehicles. The project utilizes the Arduino UNO microcontroller and Hall effect sensors for feedback, enabling precise commutation and smooth motor operation. Through meticulous circuit design and programming, the controller effectively regulates the speed and direction of the BLDC motor. The inclusion of a potentiometer for real-time speed adjustment enhances user control. It is built to design and implement a Brushless DC (BLDC) motor controller using a microcontroller, to achieve precise speed control, efficient operation, and reliable performance in various applications such as electric vehicles, robotics, and industrial automation. Future work involves optimizing the code, exploring regenerative braking features, and adapting the controller for broader electric vehicle platforms. The project sets a foundation for further refining and expanding electric vehicle technology. Overall this study provides a comprehensive investigation into the design, implementation, and performance evaluation of a microcontroller-based Brushless DC (BLDC) motor controller. It highlights the significance of closed-loop control systems in enhancing motor efficiency and responsiveness, offering practical solutions for industries requiring advanced motor control capabilities.

articleTitle: Safety Alerting and Monitoring System for Coal Mine
abstract: Mining is the process of extracting minerals like liquids, solids, or gases from the ground. Coal is used in the production of electricity, cement, steel, and various industries. However, ensuring the safety of coal mining workers in today's generation is challenging. To increase the safety of mining workers and achieve profitability while lowering costs, we need creative and innovative methodologies. The methodology is divided into two sections: one, for proposing a system to monitor mine workers and the other for overall monitoring. Safety takes precedence in any working environment, especially in mining, where extracting coal from underground presents significant risks. Despite existing precautions, accidents persist. A more effective system is needed to monitor health, temperature, water level, moisture, and gases underground. Various harmful gases like CH4, CO, S02, N02 are released during mining, severely affecting the workers' health. The environment inside the mine is hostile. A better system must be developed to meet all aspects related to the mining environment and immediately alert workers about conditions so they can rescue people from accidents. This work monitors hazardous gases, fire, moisture, temperature, and humidity. The monitoring and alerting system is driven by an Arduino micro controller for the master controller and 8051 micro controllers for slave controllers. If there is any critical state, it alerts the workers through the buzzer, and messages are sent to the supervisor immediately so they can rescue people in the mining area. To get over this problem, a wireless sensor network's application system has been proposed.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection in Video Surveillance for Unusual Behavior Identification
abstract: “Anomaly detection in video surveillance” identifies unusual behavior in camera footage, boosting security. State-of-the-art methods use both normal and abnormal videos to train, reducing manual monitoring but potentially causing false alarms. This paper highlights a learning algorithm that trains on both normal and anomalous videos to learn to detect anomalies. This paper employs 3D ResNet-101 for feature extraction, facilitating the capture of rich spatiotemporal information from the videos. Subsequently, it uses the MIL framework with weakly labeled training data. Within this approach, individual video segments are viewed as instances, and regular and anomalous videos are viewed as bags. In order to automatically create a deep anomaly ranking model, we finally include multiple instance learning (MIL). This model assigns high anomaly scores to video segments exhibiting unusual behavior, enabling the effective identification of potential security threats.

articleTitle: Low Power 3-Bit Decoder Design using Memristor
abstract: In the pursuit of energy-efficient and innovative VLSI designs, the integration of memristor technology has emerged as a promising avenue. This project endeavours to explore the design and implementation of a low-power 3-bit decoder utilizing memristor devices. The memristor's unique properties, such as non-volatility and low energy consumption, offer an unprecedented opportunity for advancing VLSI circuits. The proposed 3-bit decoder leverages memristors to decode a 3-bit binary input into a unique 3-bit output representation, enabling a compact and efficient decoding solution. Throughout the project, various low-power design methodologies and memristor-based optimization techniques are investigated to minimize power consumption while ensuring reliable performance. This project not only delves into the theoretical underpinnings of memristor technology but also embraces practical challenges in designing memristor-based VLSI circuits. Extensive simulations and verification processes are conducted to validate the decoder's correctness and robustness. The potential applications of memristor-based decoders extend beyond this specific project, contributing to the broader exploration of memristor technologies and their integration into modern VLSI designs. The outcomes of this study will not only enrich the realm of VLSI but also pave the way for more energy-efficient and technologically advanced integrated circuits, propelling the semiconductor industry towards a sustainable and innovative future.

articleTitle: Agriculture Voice Bot Integrated with Crop Prediction Using ML In Telugu
abstract: The “Agriculture Voice Bot Integrated with Crop Recommendation using ML in Telugu” project introduces a groundbreaking approach to support farmers through voicebased interactions, encompassing general inquiries and personalized crop recommendations. By harnessing conversational chatbot technology, this system enables farmers to voice their queries and receive interactive responses, akin to widely-used voice assistants such as Siri, Cortana, Watson, and Alexa. Specifically tailored for the agricultural domain, this voice-enabled assistant provides intuitive assistance to farmers, empowering them to enhance farming techniques, increase agricultural productivity, and access crop forecasting assistance. Utilizing Natural Language Processing (NLP), the system analyzes user queries, extracts pertinent keywords, and retrieves precise responses from an extensive Knowledge Base. Furthermore, to facilitate communication in Telugu, the system incorporates Google Text-to-Speech (gTTS) technology, enabling the generation of voice responses in the Telugu language. By integrating Machine Learning (ML) techniques and offering responses in Telugu, this project aims to revolutionize agricultural assistance, providing a user-friendly and effective solution tailored to the needs of farmers.

articleTitle: All Stability Region Based Tuning of PR Controller for Stable Processes
abstract: A graphical tuning method for proportional-resonant (PR) controller based on concept of root crossing boundaries is proposed. Controller settings are obtained by computing the centroid of convex stability boundary locus in the plane of controller parameters. Novelty of proposed method is that it is simple and can be used for a wide class of processes. Furthermore, it is observed that improved closed loop performance is achieved as compared to the recently reported approaches. Usefulness of the proposed tuning method is illustrated by simulation study conducted on plants with and without time delay.

articleTitle: Internet of Things (IoT)-based Speed Control and Characteristics Monitoring for a BLDC-Motor in the Electric Vehicles with the help of MATLAB and Thing-Speak
abstract: BLDC motors are very popular in Electric Vehicles. In recent days, the Internet of Things is an emerging technology, that solves great difficulties in Electric vehicle control and monitoring Things Speak can resolve different fields of research like unmanned vehicles, VANET, Automatic traffic control, and smart vehicles. In this paper, we control BLDC speed with the help of Hall effect sensors, for this reference speed and load torque are read from Thing Speak, later after controlling the BLDC, its characteristics are monitored again in Thing Speak

articleTitle: Thermal-Resilient Antenna Design for Wireless Communication
abstract: The effect of ambient temperature on the wireless frequency range, focusing on minimizing signal loss, is discussed in the paper. The antenna under investigation operates within two frequency bands: 1.7-4 GHz and 5.1-8.8 GHz, with respective bandwidths of 2.3 GHz and 3.7 GHz. Ambient temperature variations can significantly impact the performance of wireless communication systems, leading to signal degradation and reduced range. The study investigates how temperature changes affect the antenna's resonant frequencies. The antenna's bandwidth, return loss, radiation patterns, and gain characteristics are simulated. Understanding the impact of ambient temperature on the wireless frequency range is crucial for designing robust communication systems capable of maintaining minimal signal loss under varying environmental conditions.

articleTitle: Philippine Region-Based Food and Nutrition Cross-Reference Using Fine-Tuned Generative ChatBot
abstract: This paper describes the development of a Large Language Model Chatbot for Philippine Food and Nutrition knowledge base. The objective is to associate the region or province of origin of any available food item in the country to the nutrients contained and the nutritional benefits to the human body, considering the build of the knowledge base coming from 30 web sites or sources. Three models have been used to test and evaluate the performance in accomplishing the task. In the training and fine-tuning efficiency, the Meta Llama 2 7B HF model is the most efficient when varying the training epochs from 1 through 5; but based on evaluation metrics of BERTScore, ROUGE Score and GLEU, the Meta Llama 3 7B Instruct model obtained the highest scores, and the highest acceptance score when tested on 100 pairs of question-and-answer with ground truths. Further demonstration of the chatbot revealed that the objective has been achieved in most query attempts during the testing phase of the development.

articleTitle: Coding Solutions for Robust Performance in Wireless Systems
abstract: Wi-Fi structures require reliable coding solutions to ensure robust overall performance. Latest advances in wireless technologies have accelerated the want for reliable coding strategies to catch up on signal losses because of shadowing, fading, and imperfect channel situations. Traditional coding techniques, together with forward mistakes correction (FEC) and variety coding, conflict to hold strong performance underneath challenging conditions. New coding strategies are needed to ensure a reliable Wi-Fi communique in difficult propagation environments. Recent research in coding answers for robust wireless systems has explored a selection of methods, such as faster codes, Low-Density Parity-test (LDPC) codes, and area-time coding. LDPC codes offer extended code lengths, which boosts coding benefits and features quite low computational complexity. Area-time codes are a block coding method that improves blunder resilience by utilizing a couple of antennas and transmitting the identical sign in more than one direction simultaneously. These coding answers were implemented to provide improved overall performance in diverse Wi-Fi systems, which include cell, WLAN, and satellite TV for PC communiqué networks. Particularly, turbo codes, LDPC codes, and area-time codes have been used effectively in WLAN networks to reduce channel mistakes and growth records prices, in addition to in mobile networks to enhance spectral efficiency and offer better throughput.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Enhanced Signal Integrity Analysis for High-Frequency Bio-Sensing Circuits
abstract: Complex approaches for signal integrity analysis in high-frequency bio-sensing circuits have been developed. This article describes “Machine Learning-Enhanced Signal Integrity Analysis.” It analyses data using random forests, support vector machines, and recurrent neural networks. We compare the proposed technique to Fourier transform, Butterworth filtering, TDR, eye diagram analysis, correlation, and power spectral density to evaluate its efficacy. Precision distribution pie charts, memory distribution violin plots, F1 score distribution box plots, and accuracy comparison scatter plots can highlight the difference. These images demonstrate how successfully the recommended technique removes tiny characteristics from high-frequency bio-sensing data. The accuracy pie chart and memory violin plot demonstrate the approach's success in discovering pleasant experiences. But the false-negative rate demonstrates how effectively it finds false positives. Precision and mental balance are shown by the F1 score box plot, while the accuracy scatter plot compares all data points. Machine learning outperforms earlier approaches in accuracy, precision, memory, and F1 score. Notably, the suggested approach displays proactive error correction methods and flexibility to varying signal circumstances. It also demonstrates computational efficiency by drastically cutting down on training and inference durations in comparison to more conventional approaches. Finally, the provided machine learning-enhanced method not only improves signal integrity analysis in high-frequency bio-sensing circuits, but also establishes a new benchmark in terms of precision, robustness, and versatility. These results highlight the revolutionary potential of applying machine learning to biomedical engineering problems, opening the door to better diagnostics and real-time monitoring in settings with high-frequency signals.

articleTitle: Fake News Detection for COVID-19 Using PySpark Framework MLlib
abstract: Besides causing a very severe health crisis for the whole world, the COVID-19 epidemic has speeded the spread of fake news and false information. Solving false news problems is important in these time-sensitive conditions to provide correct information and guarantee people's safety. This work aims to use PySpark, a distributed data processing platform, to create a prediction model for identifying COVID-19 fake news. The experiments are conducted on a dataset sourced from Kaggle and a prediction model is created using PySpark's machine learning libraries, such as MLlib and SparkML, to classify news articles as real or false. Different classification methods, such as logistic regression, decision trees, and random forests, are researched and improved for the best performance. The accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score of the model are assessed using relevant measures, confirming its efficacy in detecting bogus news. The best results were achieved by the logistic regression classifier which achieved accuracy and F-measure of 0.9.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis of Financial News and its Impact on the Stock Market
abstract: In recent years, there has been significant interest and innovation in combining sentiment analysis techniques with financial markets. This study provides a concise review of the literature on sentiment analysis applied to stock market news and its subsequent impact on market behavior. The research methodology involved extracting data from stock market news sources and using sentiment analysis, specifically the NLTK Vader tool, to categorize this information. The focus was on understanding how sentiment analysis influences stock market dynamics. Additionally, the study included the use of machine learning models to further explore these relationships. The findings contribute to our comprehension of how sentiment analysis can classify stock market data and its influence on market behavior, highlighting the potential applications of sentiment analysis in financial decision-making processes. This research emphasizes the importance of combining sentiment analysis techniques with machine learning algorithms like Random Forest, ARIMA and LSTM to gain insights into the complex interplay between news sentiment and stock market movements.
